long_biography.plain_text:
After early roles at Paribas and Renault Finance, Sabrier assumed responsibility for a small family-owned fund manager at age 23. He added hedge funds in the 1980s, began proprietary buyout investing, acquired and sold a Swiss bank, and helped establish an early European fund-of-funds vehicle. These moves shifted Unigestion beyond its original bond-market focus and built an international alternatives franchise.

Sabrier placed control of the group with Famsa, a charitable foundation designed for patient ownership. A strategic combination with Sagard extended that model into a larger mid-market investment platform, where he remains a senior governor. His public work also includes the children's charity he established and MAMCO, Geneva's modern-art museum, which he helped create.
